slides.texte_overlay:
5 posture slips that make
you look anxious
Slip 1: stiff, locked knees. Standing rigid for a long time makes you look tense and uncomfortable. Keep a slight bend in your knees and let your body breathe.
Slip 2: chin tucked into your chest. It shrinks you and muffles your voice. Lift your chin slightly so your eyes meet people's, not the floor.
Slip 3: arms glued to your sides. Holding your arms tight against your body looks frozen. Let them hang loosely and move naturally when you talk.
Slip 4: turning your feet toward the exit. People unconsciously point their feet where they want to go. Turn them toward the person you're talking to.
Before: tense shoulders in every new room. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer mind that keeps my body relaxed.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: tense shoulders in every new room. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A calmer mind keeps my body relaxed.

slides.texte_overlay: Slip 5: sitting on your hands. It hides them and makes you look like you're holding yourself back. Rest your hands on the table or your thighs instead.
The fix: a quick body scan before any important moment. Feet, knees, shoulders, chin, hands. Thirty seconds of checking makes you look calm all evening.
